summary_for_children: Ar-Rum means The Romans. It begins with a promise that came true and points to signs of Allah: our different languages and colours, the winds, rain, and how dead earth comes back to life.
world_title: The Winds and the Colours of People
environment_concept: A market of many languages (30:22), a harbour with ships on good winds (30:46), clouds that spread and break into rain (30:48) and bare land returning to green (30:50).
architecture_and_scenery: A port town with ships, a hillside market with many voices, rain-swept hills, and a distant land of an old empire's ruins.

palette.lighting: Shifting cloud shadows and sudden sunlight after rain

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Changing World
story_library.children_narration: Surah Ar-Rum begins by referring to the Romans' defeat and future victory. It reminds us that events in the world can change. The Quran also invites us to look at the signs of creation: the changing seasons, the winds, and the return of life to the land after rain.

world_idea.title: The World Through Seasons
world_idea.description: Explore a landscape changing from dry conditions to rainfall and renewed growth. Study the historical passage through a separate illustrated map.
